sources.title: True and false interindividual differences in the physiological response to an intervention
Existence of consistent hypo- and hyperresponders to dietary cholesterol in man
High responders and low responders: factors associated with individual variation in response to standardized training

concepts.definition: A person whose measured response to a stimulus is far above that of most people.
Random day-to-day and measurement-to-measurement variation that is part of every measured change.

questions.q: Why can a hyperresponder label from one trial be wrong?
questions.a: The measured change includes random variation that can produce extreme values in people with an ordinary true response.

questions.q: How can one test whether individual differences in response are real?
questions.a: Repeat the intervention in the same people, or compare the spread of changes with a control group.
